explanation: Twelve months of 30 days are followed by Pagume, a short month of five days, or six in a leap year. Ethiopian year numbers also run seven to eight years behind the Gregorian count.

claims.text: The Ethiopian calendar has 12 months of 30 days followed by Pagume, a month of five days, or six in a leap year.
Ethiopian calendar years are numbered seven or eight years behind Gregorian years.
